content.question: What does `event.target.value` represent for the text input above?

options.text: The current text in the input that produced the event.
The React component's entire state object.
The name of the parent component.

feedback.correct: The target is the element involved in the event, and its value is the current input value.
feedback.incorrect: The target is the element involved in the event, and its value is the current input value.

activities.title: Stop propagation when the boundary matters

content.title: Stop propagation when the boundary matters

content.question:
A developer adds `onClick` to a wrapper around every button and then adds more special cases every time a nested control behaves strangely.

What is the better first question?

options.text: Which event handlers are receiving the propagated event, and which element actually owns the interaction?
How many more wrappers can we add?
Can we remove every button and use text?

feedback.correct: Event propagation can be useful, but it can also create surprising interactions. Trace which element received the event and which ancestors also react.
feedback.incorrect: Event propagation can be useful, but it can also create surprising interactions. Trace which element received the event and which ancestors also react.

content.title: Event handler versus effect

content.question: A nested button triggers both its own action and a parent's action. What concept should you investigate first?

feedback.correct: The symptom starts inside the browser event path. Understand propagation before changing unrelated architecture.
feedback.incorrect: The symptom starts inside the browser event path. Understand propagation before changing unrelated architecture.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** An event has both a source and a path. A handler can use event data, and a parent can receive a propagated event unless the child stops it.
**Senior habit:** When an interaction seems to fire twice, inspect the event path before blaming React state.
nextSteps: Use an event object to read input data and stop a child interaction from triggering an unwanted parent action.
